# bpc157pens.com

> Research education about BPC-157 pens and vials: what the pre-filled pen format is, how it compares with liquid and freeze-dried vials, how to store both, what a certificate of analysis (COA) should show, and BPC-157's U.S. regulatory status. Every claim is cited to peer-reviewed studies or official regulator pages. Last reviewed November 15, 2026.

Key facts:

- BPC-157 (Body Protection Compound 157) is a synthetic 15-amino-acid peptide, sequence GEPPPGKPADDAGLV, formula C62H98N16O22, molecular weight 1419.5 g/mol, CAS 137525-51-0.
- BPC-157 is not FDA-approved for any use. In 2023 FDA listed it among compounding substances that may present significant safety risks. On July 23, 2026 an FDA advisory committee voted 8-6 (one abstention) to recommend adding it to the 503A bulks list; FDA has not finalized any change.
- Evidence is mostly cell and animal research. A 2026 systematic review found three small human studies (30 participants in total) and rated certainty as very low.
- WADA prohibits BPC-157 at all times under S0 (non-approved substances). The U.S. Department of Defense also prohibits it.
- A BPC-157 pen is a pre-filled 3 mL cartridge pen with a dial, holding BPC-157 already in solution. Palm Beach Vitality sells 10 mg (about 3.33 mg/mL) and 20 mg (about 6.67 mg/mL) pens.
- Palm Beach Vitality's BPC-157 liquid vials hold 10 mL at 1 mg/mL (10 mg) or 2 mg/mL (20 mg).
- Storage per the seller: 2-8 °C (36-46 °F), protect from light, do not freeze; practical shelf life 4-6 weeks for pens and 16-20 weeks for liquid vials.
- Products are sold for laboratory research use only, ship to U.S. addresses only, and have lot-specific COAs available on request.
- bpc157pens.com does not provide dosing or usage instructions.

Disclosure: bpc157pens.com is owned by the same company as Palm Beach Vitality (palmbeach-vitality.store), the store it links to.
